Abstract.AbstractText: Cyclosporin A (CsA) is a well-known immunosuppressant that is used against steroid-resistant asthma. Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) and type 2 helper T (Th2) cells produce Th2 cytokines including IL-5 and play important roles in asthma pathogenesis. Here, we studied the effects of CsA in allergen-induced lung inflammation in mice and found that CsA decreased the number of lung ILC2s and attenuated papain-induced activation of ILC2s accompanied with IL-5 expression. The ILC2 suppression mediated by CsA was not observed in culture or in lymphocyte-deficient Rag2(-/-) mice. Thus, we propose a new suppressive effect of CsA, i.e., administration of CsA indirectly suppresses maintenance and activation of lung ILC2s in addition to direct suppression of T-cell activation and cytokine production.
